words.enDefinition: how a venture creates value and earns money

examples.en: Our bike repair project changed its business model after students asked for home visits.
examples.zh: 有同学提出上门需求后，我们的自行车维修项目调整了「商业模式」。

examples.en: At the showcase, Jia described a business model that relied on renting equipment by the day.
examples.zh: 在展示会上，佳介绍了一种靠按天出租设备赚钱的「商业模式」。

words.enDefinition: a one-page framework for mapping how a venture works

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to complete a Business Model Canvas for the student laundry service.
examples.zh: 导师让我们为学生洗衣服务填写一张「商业模式画布」。

examples.en: The Business Model Canvas helped the team see where its suppliers fit into the plan.
examples.zh: 「商业模式画布」帮助小组看清供应商在计划中扮演的角色。

collocations: fill in a Business Model Canvas

words.enDefinition: the benefit an offering promises to people considering it

examples.en: Our value proposition is convenient laptop repairs while students are already on campus for class.
examples.zh: 我们的「价值主张」是同学们来学校上课时，就能顺便修电脑。

examples.en: The judges asked why evening pickup mattered enough to be part of our value proposition.
examples.zh: 评委问我们，为什么晚间自提重要到足以成为「价值主张」的一部分。

words.enDefinition: the ways a venture interacts with and supports customers

examples.en: The pottery team put personal help with glazing under customer relationships on its canvas.
examples.zh: 陶艺小组在画布的「客户关系」栏里填了为顾客提供上釉指导。

examples.en: Our advisor asked how customer relationships would change if the booking service became fully automated.
examples.zh: 导师问，如果预订服务完全自动化，「客户关系」会有什么变化。

words.enDefinition: the main actions a venture must carry out

examples.en: When we listed key activities, collecting and cleaning the rental mugs came before product design.
examples.zh: 列「关键业务活动」时，我们把回收和清洗租用杯子排在了产品设计之前。

examples.en: Our advisor asked which key activities the student team could realistically handle during exam week.
examples.zh: 导师问学生团队，考试周实际上还能做哪些「关键业务活动」。

words.enDefinition: the assets a venture relies on to operate

examples.en: The repair team listed its workbench and tool library as key resources for the service.
examples.zh: 维修小组把工作台和设备借用中心列为开展服务的「关键资源」。

examples.en: Losing access to the university kitchen would remove one of our key resources for catering.
examples.zh: 要是不能再用学校厨房，我们的配餐项目就会失去一项「关键资源」。

words.enDefinition: the outside relationships that help a venture operate

examples.en: On the canvas, we listed the campus print shop and the library under key partnerships.
examples.zh: 我们在画布的「关键合作关系」栏里填写了校内打印店和图书馆。

examples.en: The mentor asked which key partnerships mattered once we started taking orders across town.
examples.zh: 导师问我们，开始接城里各处的订单后，哪些「关键合作关系」会很重要。

words.enDefinition: a distinct way a venture earns money

examples.en: A repair workshop could become a second revenue stream alongside our refurbished bicycle sales.
examples.zh: 开办维修工作坊可以成为我们的第二个「收入来源」，和翻新自行车销售并行。

examples.en: During the showcase, the judges asked which revenue stream would continue over the summer break.
examples.zh: 展示期间，评委问哪个「收入来源」在暑假仍能持续。

words.enDefinition: the main costs a venture faces and how they relate

examples.en: The cost structure changed when our team replaced a rented studio with a shared workshop.
examples.zh: 团队改用共享工作坊后，「成本结构」发生了变化。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked us to explain the cost structure of a one-person campus delivery service.
examples.zh: 讲师让我们解释由一人运营的校园配送服务的「成本结构」。

words.enDefinition: how a venture plans to earn money from customers

examples.en: The design students compared two options for their revenue model: paid downloads and monthly access.
examples.zh: 设计专业的同学比较了两种「营收模式」：付费下载和按月付费使用。

examples.en: Our revenue model changed once clubs asked to pay for the whole semester in advance.
examples.zh: 有社团提出想预付一整个学期的费用后，我们调整了「营收模式」。

collocations: switch to a new revenue model

words.enDefinition: making an offering useful or beneficial to someone

examples.en: For our team, value creation meant getting borrowed equipment into students' hands between classes.
examples.zh: 对我们组而言，「价值创造」就是让学生在两节课之间就能拿到借用的器材。

examples.en: In class, we discussed how saving students a trip across campus could count as value creation.
examples.zh: 我们在课上讨论，替同学省下一趟横穿校园的路为什么也算「价值创造」。

words.enDefinition: getting the benefits of an offering to the customer

examples.en: We planned value delivery around locker pickup because many students finished class after our stall closed.
examples.zh: 很多学生下课时摊位已经收了，所以我们计划用取物柜自提来实现「价值交付」。

examples.en: The business tutor asked how home visits changed value delivery for the sewing repair project.
examples.zh: 商业课导师问，上门服务会怎样改变缝补项目的「价值交付」。

words.enDefinition: how a venture retains some benefit from what it creates

examples.en: Our group discussed value capture after deciding that local businesses could sponsor the free map.
examples.zh: 小组决定让本地商家赞助免费地图后，讨论了如何实现「价值获取」。

examples.en: The lecturer explained value capture using a refill service that charged for each jar filled.
examples.zh: 讲师以按灌装瓶数收费的补充装服务为例，解释了什么是「价值获取」。

words.enDefinition: whether a venture can sustain itself financially in practice

examples.en: At the showcase, the judges questioned business model viability once the team mentioned subsidized rent.
examples.zh: 展示会上，小组提到租金有补贴后，评委对「商业模式可行性」提出了疑问。

examples.en: Our course project assessed business model viability using separate estimates for term time and summer.
examples.zh: 课程项目分别估计学期内和暑假的情况，以评估「商业模式可行性」。

words.enDefinition: how people and processes are organized to run a venture

examples.en: Our operating model moved repairs to a shared workshop and kept collections at the stall.
examples.zh: 我们的「运营模式」调整为在共享工作坊维修，在摊位收取待修物品。

examples.en: The judges asked what the operating model looked like when both founders had morning classes.
examples.zh: 评委问，两位创办人上午都有课时，项目采用怎样的「运营模式」。

words.enDefinition: the main thing a venture provides to its customers

examples.en: The stall's core offering was a simple lunch box, with drinks available as extras.
examples.zh: 摊位的「核心产品」是简餐盒，饮品可以另点。

examples.en: Our core offering for the first term was same-day repair for torn backpacks.
examples.zh: 第一学期，我们的「核心服务」是当天修好撕破的背包。

words.enDefinition: a person or organization that pays for an offering

examples.en: For our note-sharing service, the department was the paying customer and the students used it.
examples.zh: 我们的笔记共享服务中，系里是「付费客户」，使用者是学生。

examples.en: The student bakery got its first paying customer at the residence hall's open day.
examples.zh: 学生面包坊在宿舍开放日迎来了第一位「付费客户」。

collocations: convert a trial user into a paying customer

words.enDefinition: selling products or services to other businesses

examples.en: In our business-to-business model, local cafés order printed table cards directly from the student team.
examples.zh: 在我们「面向企业客户的」模式下，本地咖啡馆直接向学生团队订购印制桌牌。

examples.en: The business-to-business side of the laundry project worked with two small guesthouses near campus.
examples.zh: 洗衣项目中「面向企业客户的」业务与校园附近的两家小旅馆合作。

words.enDefinition: selling products or services to people for personal use

examples.en: The student team pitched a business-to-consumer service that cleaned trainers for people living on campus.
examples.zh: 学生团队推介了一项「面向个人消费者的」服务，为住校的人清洗运动鞋。

examples.en: Our business-to-consumer model was designed around individual orders for custom phone cases at the market.
examples.zh: 我们「面向个人消费者的」模式以市集上的手机壳个人定制订单为主。

words.enDefinition: selling directly to shoppers without an independent retailer

examples.en: The student label chose a direct-to-consumer approach and sold its tote bags through its own website.
examples.zh: 学生品牌采用「直接面向消费者的」做法，通过自家网站卖帆布袋。

examples.en: Our direct-to-consumer sales brought the pottery team into regular contact with buyers at weekend markets.
examples.zh: 我们「直接面向消费者的」销售方式让陶艺小组经常在周末市集接触买家。

words.enDefinition: a marketplace that brings two distinct participant groups together

examples.en: The class project imagined a two-sided marketplace that connected students needing repairs with local tailors.
examples.zh: 课程项目设想了一个「双边交易平台」，把需要修补衣物的学生和本地裁缝联系起来。

examples.en: Our tutor drew a two-sided marketplace with private tutors on one side and learners on the other.
examples.zh: 导师画出一个「双边交易平台」，一边是私人辅导老师，另一边是学习者。

collocations: both sides of a two-sided marketplace

words.enDefinition: a model where customers pay periodically for continuing access

examples.en: The student design team proposed a subscription model for its library of printable revision cards.
examples.zh: 学生设计团队提出用「订阅模式」提供可打印的复习卡片库。

examples.en: Our subscription model gave residents access to shared tools for as long as they stayed subscribed.
examples.zh: 我们的「订阅模式」让住户在订阅期间都能使用共享工具。

words.zhGloss: 基础免费增值收费模式
words.enDefinition: a model with a free offering and optional paid upgrades
acceptedZhAnswers: 基础免费增值收费模式

examples.en: The student app used a freemium model with free schedules and paid exports for clubs.
examples.zh: 学生应用采用「基础免费、增值收费的模式」，日程表免费，社团需要导出时再付费。

examples.en: We sketched a freemium model where basic practice quizzes were free and detailed explanations cost extra.
examples.zh: 我们设计了「基础免费、增值收费的模式」，基础练习测验免费，详细讲解另外收费。

collocations: a freemium model with paid upgrades

words.enDefinition: a model that charges others for permission to use something

examples.en: The illustration students proposed a licensing model for cafés that wanted to print their designs on mugs.
examples.zh: 插画专业的同学为想在杯子上印图案的咖啡馆提出了「授权经营模式」。

examples.en: Our licensing model gave campus clubs permission to reuse the graphics in their own brochures.
examples.zh: 我们的「授权经营模式」允许校内社团在自家的宣传册中使用这些图案。

words.enDefinition: a model in which operators pay to use a business system and brand

examples.en: In class, we compared a franchise model with a student chain that operated every shop itself.
examples.zh: 课上，我们比较了「特许经营模式」和由学生连锁品牌自己运营所有门店的做法。

examples.en: The team described a franchise model where local operators used the same sandwich stall name and menu.
examples.zh: 小组介绍了一种「特许经营模式」，当地经营者使用统一的三明治摊位名称和菜单。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement where the supplier is paid when goods sell

examples.en: The ceramics club used a consignment model so students kept ownership of pieces until they sold.
examples.zh: 陶艺社采用「寄售模式」，作品卖出之前仍归创作的同学所有。

examples.en: Under the consignment model, the student shop sends us a share only after a bag sells.
examples.zh: 按「寄售模式」，只有帆布袋卖出后，学生商店才会把我们的份额转过来。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement where customers complete routine steps on their own

examples.en: Our self-service model lets students book a storage locker online and collect the key themselves.
examples.zh: 我们的「自助服务模式」允许同学们在线预订储物柜，并自行领钥匙。

examples.en: The mentor asked whether a self-service model would still work for students who needed help measuring.
examples.zh: 导师问，需要人帮忙测量的同学能不能使用「自助服务模式」。

words.zhGloss: 需要大量人工沟通的服务
words.enDefinition: a service involving substantial personal attention and direct interaction
acceptedZhAnswers: 需要大量人工沟通的服务

examples.en: Our high-touch service pairs each new language learner with a tutor for a planning call.
examples.zh: 我们的「需要大量人工沟通的服务」会为每位新学员安排辅导老师，先打电话商量学习计划。

examples.en: The tailoring team explained why its high-touch service required extra time for individual fittings.
examples.zh: 裁缝服务小组解释了为什么他们的「需要大量人工沟通的服务」需要为每次单独试衣留更多时间。

words.enDefinition: a choice between producing something internally and buying it externally

examples.en: The student café faced a make-or-buy decision when demand for its bread doubled in March.
examples.zh: 三月份面包需求翻倍后，学生咖啡馆面临「自制还是外购的决策」。

examples.en: We wrote a short report on the make-or-buy decision for the reusable boxes at our stall.
examples.zh: 我们写了份简短报告，讨论摊位的可重复使用餐盒该「自制还是外购」。

words.enDefinition: making a product within the venture with its own people or facilities

examples.en: In-house production let the team change the notebook covers without waiting for an outside printer.
examples.zh: 「自行生产」让小组能更换笔记本封面，无需等外部印刷商。

examples.en: Our in-house production moved into the university workshop after the craft market became a regular event.
examples.zh: 手作市集变成定期活动后，我们把「自行生产」搬到了学校工坊。

words.enDefinition: a model designed primarily around keeping costs low

examples.en: Our assignment described a cost-driven business model built around shared ovens and one standard sandwich.
examples.zh: 我们的作业介绍了一个「成本驱动型商业模式」，以共享烤箱和单一标准三明治为基础。

examples.en: The team presented a cost-driven business model for a campus shuttle with fixed pickup points.
examples.zh: 团队展示了一个采用固定上车点的校园接驳服务「成本驱动型商业模式」。

collocations: a cost-driven business model focused on efficiency

words.enDefinition: a model centered on delivering distinctive customer benefits

examples.en: The team explained its value-driven business model to judges using an example of custom fittings.
examples.zh: 团队用一对一试穿调整的例子向评委说明了「价值驱动型商业模式」。

examples.en: Our value-driven business model relied on hand-bound portfolios and offered students a choice of paper.
examples.zh: 我们的「价值驱动型商业模式」以手工装订作品集为主，并允许学生自选纸张。

collocations: a value-driven business model for custom work

words.enDefinition: a sale with no scheduled follow-up charges

examples.en: We treated each printed planner as a one-time sale, even if buyers came back later.
examples.zh: 我们把每本纸质计划本都视为「一次性销售」，即使买家之后可能再来。

examples.en: The illustrator chose a one-time sale for each download rather than charging a monthly fee.
examples.zh: 插画师决定每次下载按「一次性销售」收费，不按月收钱。

collocations: a one-time sale of a product
earn revenue from a one-time sale

words.enDefinition: income expected to repeat from ongoing customer agreements

examples.en: The student club's tool library earned recurring revenue through monthly fees for access to equipment.
examples.zh: 学生社团的工具借用中心靠按月收取使用费获得「经常性收入」。

examples.en: The mentors asked whether recurring revenue could cover rent when the team paused one-off sales.
examples.zh: 导师问，团队暂停零星销售时，能否用「经常性收入」支付租金。

words.enDefinition: income that arrives mainly at particular times of year

examples.en: The graduation photographer relied on seasonal revenue because most bookings came in May and June.
examples.zh: 毕业照摄影师主要靠「季节性收入」，因为大多数预约集中在五月和六月。

examples.en: We showed seasonal revenue separately when estimating how much the campus stall would earn each month.
examples.zh: 我们估算校园摊位每月能赚多少时，把「季节性收入」单独列了出来。

words.enDefinition: the relative shares of income from different sources

examples.en: Our revenue mix shifted toward paid repairs after the student shop stopped selling spare parts.
examples.zh: 学生商店不再卖零件后，我们的「收入构成」开始侧重付费维修。

examples.en: The team used a pie chart to show the revenue mix from leases, repairs, and lessons.
examples.zh: 团队用饼图展示租赁、维修和课程三项业务的「收入构成」。

collocations: a shift in the revenue mix

words.enDefinition: the extent to which income depends on a few sources

examples.en: Our mentor noticed high revenue concentration because one residence hall paid for nearly all the repairs.
examples.zh: 导师注意到我们的「收入集中度」很高，几乎所有维修收入都来自同一栋宿舍楼。

examples.en: The team measured revenue concentration before one large client decided whether to renew its contract.
examples.zh: 一位大客户还在考虑是否续约时，团队测算了「收入集中度」。

words.enDefinition: income earned from customers' ongoing paid access

examples.en: The music students used subscription revenue from their lesson library to pay for editing software.
examples.zh: 音乐专业的学生用课程库的「订阅收入」支付剪辑软件的费用。

examples.en: The line for subscription revenue grew when several campus clubs switched to yearly plans.
examples.zh: 几个校园社团改用年度方案后，账上的「订阅收入」增加了。

words.enDefinition: money earned by displaying or publishing paid advertisements

examples.en: Advertising revenue from two local shops helped cover the printing costs of our campus magazine.
examples.zh: 两家本地商店带来的「广告收入」分担了我们校园杂志的印刷费。

examples.en: The student podcast recorded advertising revenue separately from what it earned by selling printed guides.
examples.zh: 学生播客把「广告收入」和卖纸质指南赚的钱分别记账。

words.enDefinition: income earned by performing services for customers

examples.en: We entered the money from tailoring under service revenue and listed fabric sales separately.
examples.zh: 我们把裁缝活赚的钱计入「服务收入」，另列布料销售收入。

examples.en: The repair team estimated service revenue by counting completed jobs during the first term.
examples.zh: 维修小组根据第一学期完成的订单数量估算「服务收入」。

words.enDefinition: a fee paid to secure continued access to a professional's services

examples.en: The design student received a retainer fee to stay available for the café's menu updates.
examples.zh: 设计专业的学生收取「预聘费」，以便在咖啡馆需要更新菜单时提供服务。

examples.en: The agreement set a regular retainer fee for the tutor's availability during the semester.
examples.zh: 协议规定按期支付「预聘费」，以便这位辅导老师在本学期提供服务。

words.enDefinition: a one-off charge for getting a service ready to use

examples.en: The booking service charged a setup fee to create each club's account and import its schedule.
examples.zh: 预订服务收取一笔「开通费」，用于为各社团创建账户并导入日程。

examples.en: We waived the setup fee for the first club because its treasurer uploaded the data herself.
examples.zh: 第一个社团的财务负责人自己上传了数据，我们就免了它的「开通费」。

words.enDefinition: a charge for using an online platform or its services

examples.en: The tutoring website kept a small platform fee whenever a student booked a group lesson.
examples.zh: 每次有学生预订团体课时，家教网站会留下一小笔「平台服务费」。

examples.en: Our team counted the platform fee before estimating how much each craft seller would receive.
examples.zh: 团队估算每位手工艺卖家能拿到多少钱时，先把「平台服务费」算了进去。

words.enDefinition: the proportion of the value transacted through a platform that it earns as revenue, such as through commissions or fees

examples.en: We used the take rate to estimate what the marketplace earned from each completed booking.
examples.zh: 我们用「平台抽佣率」估算交易平台从每笔完成的预约中获得多少收入。

examples.en: The student team lowered the take rate after local makers asked to keep more of each sale.
examples.zh: 本地创作者希望每笔销售能多留一点钱，学生团队因此降低了「平台抽佣率」。

words.enDefinition: money earned by letting others use an asset for payment

examples.en: The student society reported rental income from renting out its portable speakers over the summer.
examples.zh: 学生社团上报了暑期出租便携音箱获得的「租赁收入」。

examples.en: Our projected rental income fell when the library started lending the same equipment for free.
examples.zh: 图书馆开始免费出借相同设备后，我们预计的「租赁收入」下降了。

words.enDefinition: income earned by providing what a contract specifies

examples.en: We recorded contract revenue for the posters once the university department accepted the finished work.
examples.zh: 学校相关部门验收成品后，我们把制作海报所得款项记为「合同收入」。

examples.en: The print club listed contract revenue from societies that hired it to make event programmes.
examples.zh: 印刷社团列出了为其他社团制作活动节目单获得的「合同收入」。

words.enDefinition: subscription-based income expressed as a monthly amount

examples.en: We used monthly recurring revenue to compare the subscription project before and after the summer break.
examples.zh: 我们用「月度经常性收入」比较订阅项目在暑假前后的情况。

examples.en: Jia divided the prepaid annual fee by twelve when calculating monthly recurring revenue for the class.
examples.zh: 佳在为课程计算「月度经常性收入」时，把预付年费除以了十二。

words.enDefinition: subscription-based income expressed as an annual amount

examples.en: Our pitch listed annual recurring revenue from subscriptions and reported equipment sales on a separate slide.
examples.zh: 推介展示列出了订阅带来的「年度经常性收入」，另用一页介绍设备销售。

examples.en: For the exercise, we translated all monthly subscription amounts into annual recurring revenue before comparing teams.
examples.zh: 完成练习时，我们把所有月度订阅金额都换算成「年度经常性收入」，再比较各小组。

words.enDefinition: projected annual revenue if a recent pace continues

examples.en: The lecturer warned that a busy graduation month could inflate the photographer's revenue run rate.
examples.zh: 讲师提醒，毕业季某个月特别忙，可能让摄影师的「营收年化估算值」偏高。

examples.en: We calculated a revenue run rate using April's sales and labeled the number as an estimate.
examples.zh: 我们用四月份的销售额计算「营收年化估算值」，并注明这一数字是估算值。

collocations: base the revenue run rate on recent sales

words.enDefinition: revenue in a period divided by the number of users

examples.en: The campus app's average revenue per user included revenue across both free and paying accounts.
examples.zh: 这款校园应用的「每位用户平均收入」以整个用户群为基数，包含免费和付费账户。

examples.en: Our average revenue per user fell as more students signed up for the free plan.
examples.zh: 更多学生注册免费方案后，我们的「每位用户平均收入」下降了。

collocations: an increase in average revenue per user

words.enDefinition: an hour of work that can be charged to a client

examples.en: The student designer counted the revision call as a billable hour under the project agreement.
examples.zh: 按项目协议，学生设计师把讨论修改的通话计为一小时「可计费工时」。

examples.en: Before submitting my timesheet, I checked whether an hour at the printer's counted as a billable hour.
examples.zh: 交工时表前，我核实了在印刷商那里花的一小时是否属于「可计费工时」。

words.enDefinition: the share of available working time chargeable to clients

examples.en: Billable utilization fell during the week when student designers spent several afternoons training their new members.
examples.zh: 学生设计师花了好几个下午培训新成员，那一周的「可计费工时占比」下降了。

examples.en: We included client work in billable utilization and tracked time spent cleaning equipment separately.
examples.zh: 我们把为客户做的工作算进「可计费工时占比」，另记清洁设备用掉的时间。

words.enDefinition: a project with a price agreed for the whole job

examples.en: The society chose a fixed-price project so it knew what the poster redesign would cost.
examples.zh: 社团选择了「固定价项目」，这样海报重新设计要花多少钱就有数了。

examples.en: Our fixed-price project covered two rounds of edits, with further revisions billed separately if requested.
examples.zh: 我们的「固定价项目」涵盖两轮修改，如需更多修改则另收费。

words.enDefinition: the amount charged for a day of work

examples.en: The student photographer quoted a day rate to cover the tournament from morning until evening.
examples.zh: 学生摄影师为从早到晚拍摄赛事报出了「按日收费标准」。

examples.en: We included the editor's day rate when comparing different ways to produce the short conference video.
examples.zh: 比较会议短片的不同制作方案时，我们把剪辑师的「按日收费标准」算了进去。

words.enDefinition: a business model that earns a share of transactions

examples.en: The student booking site used a commission-based model and kept a percentage of every completed booking.
examples.zh: 学生预订网站采用「佣金模式」，从每笔完成的预订中抽取一定比例。

examples.en: We compared a commission-based model with charging each seller an annual fee to use the marketplace.
examples.zh: 我们将「佣金模式」和向每位卖家收取平台年费的做法作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a factor that strongly affects how much money is earned

examples.en: The number of sessions booked was the main revenue driver for our student tutoring service.
examples.zh: 课时预订量是我们学生家教服务的主要「创收关键因素」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked which revenue driver mattered most for a repair stall with only one workbench.
examples.zh: 讲师问，维修摊只有一张工作台时，哪个「创收关键因素」影响最大。

words.enDefinition: using revenue from one offering to support a different one

examples.en: The student cinema used a cross-subsidy from weekend screenings to keep weekday tickets affordable.
examples.zh: 学生影院用周末放映的收入提供「交叉补贴」，让工作日的票价保持实惠。

examples.en: Our plan used a cross-subsidy so that full-price repairs could support a reduced rate for bursary recipients.
examples.zh: 我们计划用全价维修业务提供「交叉补贴」，让领助学金的同学能享受较低收费。

words.enDefinition: income lost through missed charges or process errors

examples.en: The tool library found revenue leakage when some paid accessories never appeared on customers' bills.
examples.zh: 工具借用中心发现，一些收费配件没有上账单，造成了「收入流失」。

examples.en: Our team spotted revenue leakage after comparing the stall's actual orders with its end-of-day receipts.
examples.zh: 把实际订单和日终收款记录一对照，小组发现了「收入流失」。

words.enDefinition: sales made to customers who come back again

examples.en: The repair stall got repeat business from students who returned with a second bike.
examples.zh: 有同学带着第二辆自行车回来维修，修车摊做成了「回头生意」。

examples.en: Our café depended on repeat business from students who came by between the same two classes.
examples.zh: 我们的咖啡馆靠同学们每次在固定两节课之间光顾的「回头生意」维持。

words.enDefinition: the rate used to charge a client for work

examples.en: The student consultancy wrote its billable rate into the agreement before anyone started the work.
examples.zh: 学生咨询团队在开工前把「对客计费费率」写进了协议。

examples.en: Our billable rate for editing covered the time we spent checking captions as well.
examples.zh: 我们剪辑服务的「对客计费费率」也适用于核对字幕所用的时间。

words.enDefinition: an optional extra offered alongside the main service

examples.en: On the booking form, express pickup appeared as a service add-on for the laundry project.
examples.zh: 洗衣项目预约表上，快速取衣列在「附加服务」一栏。

examples.en: The student photographer offered a printed album as a service add-on after each portrait session.
examples.zh: 每次人像拍摄结束后，学生摄影师会提供印制相册这项「附加服务」。

words.enDefinition: a product available on its own without the rest of an offering

examples.en: After the showcase, our team offered the meal planner as a standalone product for students.
examples.zh: 展示会结束后，小组把餐食计划表作为「独立销售的产品」提供给学生。

examples.en: The notebook started as part of a course pack and later became a standalone product.
examples.zh: 笔记本原本包含在课程套装里，后来成了「独立销售的产品」。

collocations: offer something as a standalone product

words.enDefinition: a set of products or services paid for in advance

examples.en: The student tutor sold a prepaid package of four conversation lessons at the start of term.
examples.zh: 开学时，学生辅导老师出售含四节口语课的「预付套餐」。

examples.en: We compared a prepaid package with single bookings for the campus pottery studio's open sessions.
examples.zh: 我们比较了校园陶艺工作室开放时段的「预付套餐」和单次预约。

words.enDefinition: someone who pays for an offering used by another person

examples.en: The department acted as a third-party payer for equipment that its students borrowed by the hour.
examples.zh: 学生按小时借用设备，系里作为「第三方付款方」。

examples.en: Our pitch identified the alumni fund as a third-party payer for the student's first workshop pass.
examples.zh: 我们的推介说明，校友基金是学生第一张工作坊通行证的「第三方付款方」。

words.enDefinition: a model that relies on advertising to fund access

examples.en: The campus newsletter adopted an ad-supported model, keeping subscriptions free for readers throughout the term.
examples.zh: 校园简报采用「广告支持模式」，让读者整个学期都能免费订阅。

examples.en: We discussed an ad-supported model for the free student map in our entrepreneurship seminar.
examples.zh: 创业研讨课上，我们为免费学生地图讨论了「广告支持模式」。

words.enDefinition: the published price before any negotiated or promotional adjustment

examples.en: The student print shop showed a list price for each poster size on its order form.
examples.zh: 学生打印店在订单表上列出了各尺寸海报的「标价」。

examples.en: We kept the list price unchanged and showed the club discount on a separate line.
examples.zh: 我们保持「标价」不变，另起一行列出社团折扣。

words.enDefinition: a stated price for supplying specific work or goods

examples.en: I sent the society a price quote for printing fifty programmes before it booked the hall.
examples.zh: 社团预订大厅前，我发去了印制五十份节目单的「报价」。

examples.en: The team received a price quote from the printer that included delivery to the student centre.
examples.zh: 团队收到了印刷商的「报价」，其中包括送到学生活动中心的费用。

words.enDefinition: a published schedule of standard rates for different services

examples.en: The student photographer's rate card showed separate fees for studio sessions and outdoor group portraits.
examples.zh: 学生摄影师的「收费价目表」分别列出了摄影棚拍摄和户外合影的费用。

examples.en: We updated the rate card when the campus radio station began offering shorter advertising slots.
examples.zh: 校园广播站开始提供时长更短的广告时段后，我们更新了「收费价目表」。

words.enDefinition: the initial price before extras or adjustments are added

examples.en: The base price covered a plain canvas bag, with embroidery available for an extra charge.
examples.zh: 「基础价格」包含一个素面帆布袋，刺绣需另付费。

examples.en: Our base price included a basic portrait session and one edited image for each student.
examples.zh: 我们的「基础价格」涵盖一次基本人像拍摄，并为每位同学提供一张修过的照片。

collocations: add fees to the base price

words.enDefinition: total sales revenue divided by the number of units sold

examples.en: Our average selling price rose after students bought more large prints than small ones at the fair.
examples.zh: 集市上，同学们买的大幅印刷品多于小幅印刷品，我们的「平均售价」随之上升。

examples.en: The team used average selling price to compare two months with very different sales volumes.
examples.zh: 团队用「平均售价」比较销售量差异很大的两个月。

collocations: track changes in average selling price

words.enDefinition: a single stated price covering all required charges

examples.en: The photographer offered an all-in price that covered the session, editing, and delivery of digital files.
examples.zh: 摄影师给出了「全包价」，含拍摄、修图和交付电子文件。

examples.en: We advertised an all-in price for the workshop, including materials and access to the studio.
examples.zh: 我们公布了工作坊的「全包价」，包含材料费和工作室使用费。

collocations: an all-in price for the package

words.enDefinition: setting different prices for different levels of access or quantity

examples.en: Our club booking app used tiered pricing based on the number of events a society ran.
examples.zh: 我们的社团预订应用根据社团举办的活动数量采用「分档定价」。

examples.en: The studio introduced tiered pricing so regular users could choose a plan with more workshop hours.
examples.zh: 工作室推出「分档定价」，让常来的用户可以选工作坊时长更多的方案。

words.enDefinition: charging according to how much a customer actually uses

examples.en: The student team chose usage-based pricing for lockers and measured the time each locker was occupied.
examples.zh: 学生团队为储物柜采用「按用量定价」的方式，并记录每个柜子的占用时长。

examples.en: In our project, usage-based pricing meant small societies paid only for the storage they used.
examples.zh: 在我们的项目中，「按用量定价」意味着小型社团只为实际使用的存储空间付费。

words.enDefinition: pricing based on the number of users given access

examples.en: For the booking software, per-seat pricing meant a society paid for each committee member with access.
examples.zh: 这款预订软件采用「按席位定价」，社团要为每个取得访问权限的委员付费。

examples.en: The team compared per-seat pricing with a single licence covering the whole student newspaper staff.
examples.zh: 团队将「按席位定价」与整家学生报社的员工共用一份授权的做法作比较。

words.enDefinition: charging one fixed amount for a defined service

examples.en: The student laundry shop chose flat-rate pricing for every bag within the same weight limit.
examples.zh: 学生洗衣店采用「统一费率定价」，未超过同一重量上限的每袋衣物收费相同。

examples.en: We explained that flat-rate pricing covered any repair on the repair stall's list.
examples.zh: 我们解释说，维修摊清单上的所有项目都采用「统一费率定价」。

words.enDefinition: setting a price by adding a markup to cost

examples.en: For the course exercise, we used cost-plus pricing after calculating the cost of a printed mug.
examples.zh: 课程练习里，我们算出一只印花杯的成本后，采用了「成本加成定价」。

examples.en: The workshop tutor demonstrated cost-plus pricing using the materials and labour needed for a tote bag.
examples.zh: 工作坊导师用制作帆布袋所需的材料和人工，演示了「成本加成定价」。

words.enDefinition: setting prices around the benefit customers perceive

examples.en: The student team discussed value-based pricing after club leaders described how much time the scheduling tool saved.
examples.zh: 社团负责人讲了日程工具能省多少时间后，学生团队讨论了「价值导向定价」。

examples.en: For the photo service, value-based pricing considered what same-day delivery was worth to graduating students.
examples.zh: 摄影服务用「价值导向定价」考虑当天交付对毕业生有多大的价值。

words.enDefinition: setting a single price for several items sold together

examples.en: We used bundle pricing for a sketchbook, pencils, and a ruler sold together at orientation.
examples.zh: 迎新时，我们把速写本、铅笔和尺子一起卖，采用「组合定价」。

examples.en: The pottery team compared bundle pricing for four sessions with charging for each session separately.
examples.zh: 陶艺小组比较了四节课的「组合定价」与按课单独收费。

words.enDefinition: charging for selected items individually instead of as a bundle

examples.en: At the design studio, à la carte pricing allowed clubs to buy only the services they needed.
examples.zh: 设计工作室采用「单项定价」，社团只需购买自己需要的服务。

examples.en: The editing team kept à la carte pricing for optional captions, translations, and extra revisions.
examples.zh: 剪辑小组继续对可选字幕、翻译和额外修改采用「单项定价」。

collocations: an à la carte pricing menu

words.enDefinition: the smallest amount billed even for a minor job

examples.en: The bike stall applied a minimum charge when a repair took less than ten minutes.
examples.zh: 维修不到十分钟时，自行车摊按「最低收费」收钱。

examples.en: We put the minimum charge on the notice so customers knew what a small job would cost.
examples.zh: 我们把「最低收费」写进告示，让顾客知道小活儿要花多少钱。

words.enDefinition: to set the amount due according to an item's weight

examples.en: At the campus refill stall, we price by weight because shoppers bring containers of different sizes.
examples.zh: 在校园补充装摊位，我们「按重量定价」，因为顾客带来的容器大小各异。

examples.en: The food cooperative chose to price by weight for loose apples supplied by a local farm.
examples.zh: 食品合作社决定对本地农场供应的散装苹果「按重量定价」。

collocations: price by weight rather than quantity
price by weight for loose produce

words.enDefinition: how strongly customers react to a change in price

examples.en: The team saw higher price sensitivity for ordinary printing than for same-day graduation photos.
examples.zh: 团队发现，普通打印顾客的「价格敏感度」高于当天交付的毕业照顾客。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked whether price sensitivity might change when students compared the two workshop options.
examples.zh: 讲师问，同学们比较两个工作坊方案时，「价格敏感度」会不会发生变化。

words.enDefinition: setting prices according to the quantity purchased, often with lower unit prices for larger orders

examples.en: The student printer offered volume pricing to societies that ordered several hundred leaflets at once.
examples.zh: 学生打印店为一次订购几百张传单的社团采用「按采购量定价」。

examples.en: We used volume pricing for the badges, so larger orders qualified for a lower unit price.
examples.zh: 我们的徽章采用「按采购量定价」，采购数量达到更高档时，单价会更低。

words.zhGloss: 按自己能负担的金额支付
words.enDefinition: an arrangement allowing customers to pay according to their means
acceptedZhAnswers: 按自己能负担的金额支付

examples.en: We put “Pay what you can” on the sign for our student-run repair afternoon.
examples.zh: 学生组织的下午维修活动上，我们在牌子上写了「按自己能负担的金额支付」。

examples.en: The theatre group tried a pay what you can policy for its first performance of the term.
examples.zh: 剧团在本学期首场演出试用了「按自己能负担的金额支付」的办法。

words.enDefinition: setting different prices along a scale based on the customer's circumstances, such as income

examples.en: The student tutoring group used sliding-scale pricing so participants could choose the rate that fit their income.
examples.zh: 学生辅导小组采用「按情况分档计价」，参与者可以按自己的收入选择相应价位。

examples.en: We explained sliding-scale pricing on the booking page and listed the available rates side by side.
examples.zh: 我们在预订页面说明了「按情况分档计价」，并把相应价位并排列出。

words.enDefinition: the minimum price allowed under a rule or pricing policy

examples.en: The student design team set a price floor for custom posters to cover printing and basic labour.
examples.zh: 学生设计团队为定制海报设定了「最低定价线」，用来覆盖印刷费和基本人工成本。

examples.en: During the simulation, the bakery could not sell below the price floor in its group agreement.
examples.zh: 在模拟项目中，面包坊的售价不能低于小组协议规定的「最低定价线」。

words.enDefinition: to make another party pay an increased expense

examples.en: When paper became more expensive, the print team decided to pass on the cost to customers.
examples.zh: 纸价上涨后，打印小组决定把这笔成本「转嫁」给顾客。

examples.en: The student stall chose not to pass on the cost of compostable cups during the trial.
examples.zh: 试行期间，学生摊位决定不把可堆肥杯子的成本「转嫁」给顾客。

collocations: pass on the cost to customers
pass on the cost of delivery

words.enDefinition: to cover an expense without charging it to someone else

examples.en: The club agreed to absorb the cost of extra envelopes rather than increase the mailing fee.
examples.zh: 社团同意「自行承担额外信封的成本」，不提高邮寄费。

examples.en: The repair team could absorb the cost of replacing one connector under its original quote.
examples.zh: 维修小组可以在原报价下「自行承担更换一个接头的成本」。

collocations: absorb the cost of a replacement
be able to absorb the cost

words.enDefinition: offering a temporary initial rate when something is first marketed

examples.en: The bicycle storage project used introductory pricing during its first month on campus to attract customers.
examples.zh: 自行车寄存项目入驻校园的第一个月采用「入市初期优惠定价」来吸引顾客。

examples.en: Our handout marked the end date for introductory pricing beside the studio's later standard rate.
examples.zh: 宣传单在工作室日后正常收费的旁边标出了「入市初期优惠定价」的截止日期。

words.enDefinition: charging a different rate during less busy times

examples.en: The studio tried off-peak pricing to attract pottery groups on quiet weekday mornings.
examples.zh: 工作室试用了「非高峰时段定价」，吸引陶艺小组在较空闲的工作日上午来。

examples.en: Our team compared off-peak pricing for morning rentals with the rate charged after classes.
examples.zh: 团队把早间租用的「非高峰时段定价」与下课后的收费作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the shortest amount of work time a client is billed for

examples.en: Our student consultancy listed minimum billable time on the quote for each remote support session.
examples.zh: 学生咨询团队在每次远程支持的报价上都列出了「最低计费时长」。

examples.en: The designer explained that minimum billable time covered preparation even when a call ended early.
examples.zh: 设计师解释，即便电话提前结束，「最低计费时长」也涵盖了准备工作。

collocations: a minimum billable time of one hour

words.enDefinition: to bill separately for things beyond the basic offering

examples.en: The photography team kept its basic price low and chose to charge for extras such as prints.
examples.zh: 摄影小组控制基础价格，对纸质照片等「附加项目另收费」。

examples.en: We agreed to charge for extras only when a client requested more than two edits.
examples.zh: 我们约定，只有客户要求修改超过两轮时，才对「附加项目另收费」。

collocations: charge for extras such as delivery
decide whether to charge for extras

words.enDefinition: to set a price lower than is appropriate

examples.en: The tutor asked whether we might underprice the service by leaving preparation out of the calculation.
examples.zh: 导师问，不把准备工作算进去，会不会让我们「把服务价格定得过低」。

examples.en: Our team learned how easy it was to underprice handmade notebooks when counting materials alone.
examples.zh: 我们团队了解到，只算材料，很容易「把手工笔记本的价格定得过低」。

words.expression: price yourself out of the market
words.lemma: price yourself out of the market
words.enDefinition: to charge so much that buyers choose other options
acceptedEnVariants: price yourself out of the market

examples.en: The tutor asked how you could price yourself out of the market with an expensive repair service.
examples.zh: 导师问，维修服务收费太高，怎么会让你「定价过高而失去市场」。

examples.en: In the exercise, you could price yourself out of the market even if your materials were excellent.
examples.zh: 在练习情境中，即使材料很好，也可能「因定价过高而失去市场」。

collocations: risk pricing yourself out of the market
price yourself out of the local market
avoid pricing yourself out of the market

words.enDefinition: to bill separately each time a session takes place

examples.en: The language tutors decided to charge per session so students could book without a membership.
examples.zh: 语言辅导老师决定「按次收费」，同学们不用入会就能预约。

examples.en: Our music group can charge per session even when the same club books several workshops.
examples.zh: 即使同一个社团预订多场工作坊，我们音乐小组也可「按次收费」。

collocations: charge per session rather than monthly

words.enDefinition: to decide how much to charge for something

examples.en: The team met after class to set a price for each handmade notebook on the stall.
examples.zh: 团队课后碰头，为摊位上的每本手工笔记本「确定售价」。

examples.en: Our mentor asked how we would set a price for repairs that took very different amounts of time.
examples.zh: 导师问，维修耗时差别很大时，我们怎样「确定售价」。

collocations: set a price for a product
set a price that covers costs

words.enDefinition: an agreement to hold a price for a stated period

examples.en: The printer offered a price lock for the student paper's next three monthly issues.
examples.zh: 印刷商给学生报接下来的三期月刊提供了「锁价安排」。

examples.en: We added a price lock to the quote so the club had time to approve it.
examples.zh: 我们在报价里加了「锁价安排」，让社团留有审批时间。

words.enDefinition: to maintain the same prices over a period

examples.en: The campus café found a new supplier and managed to keep prices steady through the semester.
examples.zh: 校园咖啡馆找到了新供应商，整个学期都设法「保持价格稳定」。

examples.en: We planned to keep prices steady until the next batch of notebooks arrived in April.
examples.zh: 我们计划在四月下一批笔记本到货之前「保持价格稳定」。

collocations: keep prices steady for a month

words.enDefinition: the basis used to calculate what a customer pays

examples.en: Our team used hours booked as the pricing metric for the shared workshop space.
examples.zh: 团队以预订小时数作为共享工作坊场地的「定价计量单位」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether number of projects was a fair pricing metric for the student app.
examples.zh: 导师问，用项目数作学生应用的「定价计量单位」是否公平。

words.enDefinition: the revenues and costs associated with one business unit such as a sale or customer

examples.en: Our advisor asked about unit economics before agreeing to discuss opening a second campus repair stall.
examples.zh: 导师先问清「单位经济性」，才同意讨论开第二个校园维修摊。

examples.en: The unit economics of the delivery project changed when we included each driver's waiting time.
examples.zh: 把每位司机的等待时间算进去后，配送项目的「单位经济性」发生了变化。

words.enDefinition: the quantity or package sold as one item

examples.en: For our pantry project, the unit of sale was a bag containing six apples.
examples.zh: 在我们的食品小店项目里，「销售计量单位」是一袋六个苹果。

examples.en: The instructor asked whether the unit of sale should be one notebook or a pack of three.
examples.zh: 老师问，「销售计量单位」应该是一本笔记本，还是三本一组。

words.enDefinition: a cost that would disappear if an activity stopped

examples.en: Packing supplies were an avoidable cost for the student team if it stopped offering home delivery.
examples.zh: 对学生团队来说，一旦停送上门，包装用品费用就是「可避免成本」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to identify one avoidable cost if the stall stopped opening on Fridays.
examples.zh: 导师让我们找出一项摊位周五停止营业后可以省下的「可避免成本」。

collocations: an avoidable cost of running a service

words.enDefinition: selling price per unit minus its variable cost

examples.en: Our unit contribution margin fell after we began including a printed guide with every kit.
examples.zh: 每套工具都附送纸质指南后，我们的「单位边际贡献」下降了。

examples.en: The class compared unit contribution margin for a plain notebook and one with a custom cover.
examples.zh: 同学们比较了普通笔记本和定制封面笔记本的「单位边际贡献」。

words.enDefinition: the full cost of meeting a customer's needs

examples.en: Our cost to serve rose for customers who asked the team to collect equipment off campus.
examples.zh: 对于要求团队到校外取设备的顾客，我们的「客户服务成本」上升了。

examples.en: The team estimated the cost to serve small clubs that needed help setting up online booking.
examples.zh: 团队估算了帮助小型社团设置在线预订产生的「客户服务成本」。

collocations: the cost to serve a customer segment

words.enDefinition: the cost associated with handling one order on average

examples.en: Our cost per order increased when we began adding protective packaging to every mug shipment.
examples.zh: 每单马克杯都加上防护包装后，我们的「单笔订单成本」上升了。

examples.en: The student team compared cost per order for pickup at the stall and for home delivery.
examples.zh: 学生团队比较了摊位自取和送货上门的「单笔订单成本」。

words.enDefinition: the cost incurred in receiving and processing returned items

examples.en: Each opened art kit added a returns handling cost because someone had to check every item.
examples.zh: 每退回一套已拆封的美术工具，就会产生「退货处理成本」，因为得有人逐件检查。

examples.en: We included a returns handling cost for sorting and repacking the notebooks that came back.
examples.zh: 我们把整理和重新包装退回的笔记本所需的「退货处理成本」算了进去。

collocations: the returns handling cost per item

words.enDefinition: the proportion of stock that becomes unusable or unsellable through deterioration

examples.en: The café recorded a higher spoilage rate for fresh berries than for packaged dry snacks.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆记录到新鲜浆果的「损耗率」高于包装干零食。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how a higher spoilage rate would change the cost of each box sold.
examples.zh: 导师问，较高的「损耗率」会怎样影响每卖出一盒的成本。

collocations: track changes in the spoilage rate

words.enDefinition: the share of available productive capacity actually in use

examples.en: Capacity utilization fell when the student print shop lost several large orders during exam week.
examples.zh: 考试周丢了几笔大单后，学生打印店的「产能利用率」下降了。

examples.en: We measured capacity utilization by comparing booked studio hours with the hours we could offer.
examples.zh: 我们把已预约的工作室时数和可开放的时数作比较，来计算「产能利用率」。

words.enDefinition: the average monetary value of a completed order

examples.en: Average order value rose after students began buying both the planner and the matching stickers.
examples.zh: 学生开始把计划本和配套贴纸一起买后，「平均客单价」上升了。

examples.en: The class compared average order value for the online stationery shop and its campus stall.
examples.zh: 班上比较了文具网店和校园摊位的「平均客单价」。

collocations: a rise in average order value

words.enDefinition: the average cost of gaining one new customer

examples.en: Our tutor asked why customer acquisition cost rose after the student café paid for local advertising.
examples.zh: 学生咖啡馆付费做本地广告后，导师问为什么「获客成本」上升了。

examples.en: The small print shop calculated customer acquisition cost using the expenses linked to finding new buyers.
examples.zh: 小型打印店根据寻找新买家的相关开支计算「获客成本」。

words.enDefinition: an estimate of the economic value a business expects from a customer over the entire relationship, sometimes based on revenue and sometimes on profit

examples.en: Our team estimated customer lifetime value for students likely to keep using the equipment lending service.
examples.zh: 团队估算了可能继续使用设备借用服务的学生的「客户终身价值」。

examples.en: The tutor said our customer lifetime value estimate assumed members would stay for three academic terms.
examples.zh: 导师说，我们估算「客户终身价值」时假设会员会留下三个学期。

collocations: compare customer lifetime value across groups

words.enDefinition: time needed for a new customer to contribute enough to recover acquisition costs

examples.en: The student team estimated the CAC payback period using the monthly profit contribution from each subscription.
examples.zh: 学生团队按每份订阅每月带来的利润贡献估算「获客成本回收期」。

examples.en: The CAC payback period became longer when we reduced the monthly price of equipment access.
examples.zh: 调低设备使用月费后，「获客成本回收期」变长了。

words.enDefinition: a study of where total revenue equals total cost

examples.en: Our break-even analysis showed how many reusable mugs the stall needed to sell before covering costs.
examples.zh: 我们的「盈亏平衡分析」显示，摊位要卖多少只可重复使用的杯子才能覆盖成本。

examples.en: The lecturer used break-even analysis to compare a permanent workshop with a weekend repair stall.
examples.zh: 讲师用「盈亏平衡分析」比较常设工坊和周末维修摊。

collocations: a break-even analysis for a new product

words.enDefinition: the amount of sales revenue needed to cover total costs

examples.en: Our projected break-even revenue increased when we moved the photography project into a rented studio.
examples.zh: 摄影项目搬进租来的工作室后，我们预计的「盈亏平衡销售额」提高了。

examples.en: We stated break-even revenue in pounds so the judges could compare it with our sales forecast.
examples.zh: 我们用英镑表示「盈亏平衡销售额」，方便评委拿它和销售预测比较。

words.enDefinition: a graph showing where total cost and revenue lines cross

examples.en: The break-even chart showed revenue crossing the total cost line at sixty orders in our example.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子里，「盈亏平衡图」显示收入线在六十单处与总成本线相交。

examples.en: We added a break-even chart to show what higher workshop rent would change in the model.
examples.zh: 我们加了一张「盈亏平衡图」，展示工作坊租金上涨会让模型发生什么变化。

collocations: plot fixed costs on a break-even chart

words.enDefinition: how long it takes for cumulative revenue to cover cumulative costs

examples.en: We estimated the time to break even for a campus photo booth with an upfront equipment cost.
examples.zh: 我们为需要预付设备成本的校园自拍亭估算了「盈亏平衡所需时间」。

examples.en: Our time to break even increased when the team delayed the first set of public workshops.
examples.zh: 团队推迟首批公开工作坊后，我们达到「盈亏平衡所需的时间」变长了。

collocations: shorten the time to break even

words.enDefinition: to earn just enough to cover the total costs

examples.en: The student bakery expected to break even if it sold every loaf at the fair.
examples.zh: 学生面包坊预计，只要集市上每条面包都卖出去，就能做到「不盈不亏」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the laundry service could break even during the quiet summer months.
examples.zh: 导师问，洗衣服务在清淡的夏季能不能做到「不盈不亏」。

words.enDefinition: to earn more than the total cost of doing business

examples.en: The student repair stall began to turn a profit after it moved into a shared workspace.
examples.zh: 学生维修摊搬进共享工作空间后，开始「实现盈利」。

examples.en: Our theatre group hoped to turn a profit after paying for the venue and printed programmes.
examples.zh: 剧团希望付完场地费和节目单印刷费后仍能「实现盈利」。

words.enDefinition: to run a venture while its costs exceed revenue

examples.en: The campus café could operate at a loss during exam week because very few students visited.
examples.zh: 考试周过来的人很少，校园咖啡馆可能会「亏损运营」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how long the project could operate at a loss before needing more support.
examples.zh: 导师问，项目可以「亏损运营」多久才需要更多支持。

collocations: continue to operate at a loss
operate at a loss for a month

words.enDefinition: lower average costs achieved as output expands

examples.en: Our student print shop gained economies of scale by spreading setup costs over more notebooks.
examples.zh: 学生打印店把开印成本分摊到更多笔记本上，获得了「规模经济」效应。

examples.en: The tutor asked why economies of scale might be harder to achieve for individual music lessons.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么一对一音乐课可能更难实现「规模经济」。

words.enDefinition: extra profit attributable to a specific change in activity

examples.en: We estimated incremental profit from opening the stall on Fridays after accounting for extra labour.
examples.zh: 把额外人工算进去后，我们估算了周五出摊能带来的「增量利润」。

examples.en: The team found little incremental profit from delivery once it included the cost of packaging.
examples.zh: 团队发现，把包装成本算进去后，配送带来的「增量利润」很少。

words.enDefinition: testing how model results change when assumptions are varied

examples.en: Our sensitivity analysis showed how the profit estimate changed as the price of paper increased.
examples.zh: 我们的「敏感性分析」显示，随着纸价上涨，利润估计值会如何变化。

examples.en: The team used sensitivity analysis to find which cost assumptions mattered most for the repair project.
examples.zh: 团队用「敏感性分析」找出哪些成本假设对维修项目影响最大。

words.enDefinition: a plausible outcome worse than the main forecast

examples.en: In our downside scenario, fewer societies rented speakers and several large bookings moved to next term.
examples.zh: 我们的「不利情景」是假设租音箱的社团变少，几笔大单还推迟到下学期。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether we had included a downside scenario for a semester with weak demand.
examples.zh: 导师问，我们有没有纳入一个学期需求低迷的「不利情景」。

words.enDefinition: a plausible outcome better than the main forecast

examples.en: In the upside scenario, the campus shop stocked our bags and ordered a second batch.
examples.zh: 在「有利情景」中，校园商店上架了我们的包，还订了第二批。

examples.en: Our upside scenario assumed that schools would book more group sessions than the original estimate.
examples.zh: 我们的「有利情景」假设各学校预订的团体课会比原先估计的多。

collocations: run the numbers for an upside scenario

words.enDefinition: comparing outcomes under different plausible sets of assumptions

examples.en: We used scenario analysis to compare a busy summer market with a term of unusually low turnout.
examples.zh: 我们用「情景分析」比较了客流旺盛的夏季市集与客流异常低迷的学期。

examples.en: In our scenario analysis, each case used a different combination of rent, staffing, and order volume.
examples.zh: 在我们的「情景分析」中，每个情景都采用不同的租金、人员配置和订单量组合。

words.enDefinition: the proportions in which different products or services are sold

examples.en: Our sales mix shifted toward smaller notebooks because they could be carried easily around campus.
examples.zh: 小号笔记本在校园里好带，我们的「销量构成」因此更偏向这一规格。

examples.en: The model showed that a change in sales mix could raise profits without increasing total orders.
examples.zh: 模型显示，即使总订单量不变，「销量构成」的变化也可能提高利润。

collocations: a shift in the sales mix

words.enDefinition: the percentage of revenue a venture aims to retain as profit

examples.en: Our team checked the target margin before asking the printer for another notebook sample.
examples.zh: 小组请印刷商再打一本样之前，先核对了「目标利润率」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked what selling price would meet our target margin in the campus café exercise.
examples.zh: 在校园咖啡馆练习中，讲师问怎样的售价才能达到我们的「目标利润率」。

words.enDefinition: an estimate of expenses expected over a future period

examples.en: We updated the cost forecast after the workshop gave us a new quote for evening hire.
examples.zh: 工作室给出新的晚间租用报价后，我们更新了「成本预测」。

examples.en: The judges asked whether the cost forecast included tool maintenance after the first semester.
examples.zh: 评委问，「成本预测」有没有算上第一学期之后的工具维护。

words.enDefinition: the total of direct expenses and allocated indirect costs

examples.en: Our fully loaded cost for the workshop included materials, tutor time, and a share of the rent.
examples.zh: 工作坊「含间接费用的总成本」包括材料、导师工时和分摊的租金。

examples.en: The team calculated the fully loaded cost of each lesson before presenting the model to classmates.
examples.zh: 团队算出每一节课「含间接费用的总成本」后，才向同学展示商业模型。

collocations: estimate the fully loaded cost per hour

words.enDefinition: the amount by which revenue falls below expectations

examples.en: We faced a revenue shortfall when half of the booked workshops were cancelled during exams.
examples.zh: 考试期间，约好的一半工作坊取消了，我们出现了「营收缺口」。

examples.en: The team tracked the revenue shortfall against its original forecast for the first six weeks.
examples.zh: 团队参照原先的预测，记录了头六周的「营收缺口」。

words.enDefinition: the amount of work time needed for each produced unit

examples.en: The team tracked labor hours per unit while making its first batch of reusable notebook covers.
examples.zh: 团队制作首批可反复使用的笔记本封套时，记录了「单位人工工时」。

examples.en: We used labor hours per unit to compare hand assembly with jobs done in the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们用「单位人工工时」比较手工组装和在工作坊完成的工序。

collocations: record average labor hours per unit

words.enDefinition: a level of activity that triggers a change in terms or costs

examples.en: The supplier set a volume threshold of one hundred bags before offering the lower price.
examples.zh: 供应商把「数量门槛」定为一百个袋子，达到才给较低价格。

examples.en: We reached the volume threshold and had to move production into a bigger campus workshop.
examples.zh: 我们达到了「数量门槛」，不得不把生产搬到校园里更大的工作坊。

words.enDefinition: the profit a venture earns from serving a particular customer

examples.en: We checked customer profitability after noticing that some large orders needed repeated visits for alterations.
examples.zh: 发现一些大单得反复上门修改后，我们检查了「客户盈利性」。

examples.en: The tutor explained customer profitability using the revenue and service costs of two typical club accounts.
examples.zh: 导师用两个典型社团客户的收入和服务成本解释了「客户盈利性」。
